channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold edges lower to near $4,150 on US–Iran peace uncertainty, hawkish Fed signals
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) trades with mild losses around $4,155 during the early Asian session on Monday. Traders continue to assess the developments surrounding the US-Iran peace talks in Switzerland.

item.title: WTI rises nearly 2% on Strait of Hormuz closure, shaky peace talks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the US oil benchmark – opened Monday’s Asian trading with an over $1 bullish gap, retesting the $78 mark, nearly up 2% in early dealings.

item.title: British Pound declines to near 1.3200 as UK PM Starmer expected to resign
item.description: The GBP/USD pair faces some selling pressure near 1.3210 during the early Asian trading hours on Monday, pressured by UK political uncertainty.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles near 161.50 amid strained US-Iran peace talks
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is facing fresh headwinds and looking to resume its downside against the US Dollar (USD) as a new week kicks off in Asia on Monday.

item.title: Australian Dollar softens to near 0.7000 as US-Iran talks stall
item.description: The AUD/USD pair declines to around 0.7005 during the early Asian session on Monday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) amid risk-off sentiment. Traders will closely monitor the developments surrounding the US-Iran peace deal.

item.title: United Kingdom PM Starmer weighs political future, set to announce exit plan on Monday
item.description: Citing a source with knowledge of the matter, Reuters reported on Monday that the United Kingdom (UK) Prime Minister (PM) Keir Starmer was reassessing his political future on Sunday after rival Andy Burnham's decisive parliamentary election victory prompted additional ministers from the governing La

item.title: US-Iran updates: Iranian negotiators suspend high-stakes talks with US in Switzerland
item.description: Here’s a brief recap of the key developments in the US-Iran geopolitical front that occurred over the weekend, especially after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday over Israel's attacks on Lebanon, and amid renewed peace talks in Switzerland.

item.title: Breaking: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz amid ceasefire deal violation
item.description: Iran says it is closing the Strait of Hormuz after accusing the United States (US) and Israel of violating the ceasefire. According to Iran, the decision came over the continued Israeli strikes in Lebanon.

item.title: Brent at $80: Did the market buy the Iran deal twice?
item.description: Brent is back near $80 and West Texas Intermediate near $77, which means the Oil market has handed back almost the entire premium it built over nearly four months of open war with Iran.

item.title: The Canadian Dollar ditches Crude Oil for Gold
item.description: The textbook calls the Canadian Dollar a petro-currency, which means that with a Middle East war keeping Crude Oil bid, the Loonie should be holding its own.

item.title: The Euro sinks on its own rate hike
item.description: The Euro did something this week that ought to be impossible: it fell in the same fortnight the European Central Bank (ECB) delivered its first interest rate hike since 2023.

item.title: The Australian Dollar looks for an excuse to break ranks
item.description: The Australian Dollar spent this week as a passenger in someone else's trade.

item.title: Gold answers to the Fed, not the fear
item.description: Gold is supposed to be the asset you want when the world looks dangerous, which makes this week's price action quietly remarkable.

item.title: The US Dollar remembers how to rally
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) spent the back half of this week doing something most desks had written off six months ago: rallying on the prospect of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US Dollar loses momentum ahead of key US inflation data
item.description: The week ahead will bring a fresh test for major currency pairs as investors digest the first Federal Reserve (Fed) policy decision under Chair Kevin Warsh and look ahead to the United States (US) Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, global PMI releases, and central-bank commentary.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG slides below 200-day SMA, bears target $61
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price tumbles for the third consecutive trading day, down over 3.32% on Friday, courtesy of broad US Dollar (USD) strength and rising US Treasury yields, which have aimed higher since Wednesday amid the Fed's hawkish tilt.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Uptrend intact as bulls eye 1.4200
item.description: The USD/CAD pair rises during the North American session, up 0.27% on Friday and over 1.34% for the week, with the pair remaining upward-biased and set to test higher prices seen last year. At the time of writing, the pair trades at 1.4175, after bouncing off daily lows of 1.4131.

item.title: Australian Dollar trades little changed as hawkish Fed and RBA outlooks collide
item.description: AUD/USD trades little changed on Friday as hawkish policy signals from both the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) offset each other, keeping the pair range-bound despite a modest pullback in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Gold price extends selloff as Fed repricing lifts USD and yields
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price edges lower by some 1.69% on Friday, poised to end with losses for the third consecutive week.At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades at $4,147, weighed by overall US Dollar strength sparked by the Federal Reserve's (Fed) decision to keep interest rates higher for longer.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Pair slumps further below 200-day SMA, eyes on 0.5700
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) dives for the third consecutive day on Friday, down in the week by over 1.48%, after hitting two-month lows of 0.5722 against the Greenback. The NZD/USD pair trades at 0.5738, down 0.25% on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen pares losses as US Dollar momentum fades despite hawkish Fed stance
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades near 161.00 on Friday, easing slightly after reaching a two-year high of 161.81 on Thursday, and breaking a five-day winning streak for the US Dollar (USD).The Japanese Yen (JPY) remains fragile as pressure mounts over a possible new intervention by authorities to strengthen

item.title: Swiss Franc sinks by design, not by peace
item.description: The Swiss Franc is the weakest major into the weekly close, dragging USD/CHF to a fresh high for the year. The tidy explanation is a wartime safe-haven bid unwinding now that the US and Iran have struck a deal; the trouble is that the Franc was never much of a haven in this war.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: RSI nears overbought territory as the pair climbs to near seven-month highs
item.description: USD/CHF extends gains on Friday even as the US Dollar (USD) eases slightly after rising to more than one-year highs. Diverging monetary policy expectations between the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Swiss National Bank (SNB) keep demand tilted toward the US Dollar over the Swiss Franc (CHF).

item.title: New Zealand Dollar extends decline as Fed tightening expectations support US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5740 at the time of writing on Friday, down 0.28% on the day, as the US Dollar (USD) continues to benefit from expectations of a restrictive monetary policy stance in the United States (US).

item.title: British Pound rebounds as holiday-thinned trade slows USD bulls
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) recovers some ground after nearing a three-month low on Friday at 1.3163, sponsored by the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish tilt, but edges up 0.18% amid thin trading conditions due to a holiday in the US.

item.title: Euro steadies as the US Dollar eases, but hawkish Fed bets limit upside
item.description: EUR/USD stages a rebound on Friday as a pullback in the US Dollar (USD) helps the Euro (EUR) stabilize after recent losses. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1470 after bouncing from a three-month low of 1.1417 touched earlier in the day.

item.title: Crude Oil has the right glut on the wrong calendar
item.description: The Crude Oil market has spent the week busily unwinding a war that has not actually been settled.

item.title: Iran confirms Switzerland meeting with US was postponed, but MOU was signed digitally
item.description: Iran’s Foreign Ministry confirmed on Friday that a planned meeting in Switzerland with US officials had been postponed, adding that preparations are already underway for a new meeting in the coming days, Reuters reported.

item.title: Euro: Limited upside as policy diverges – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s research suggests EUR/USD upside is constrained in coming months by interest rate differentials and relative growth. The European Central Bank is seen closer to the end of its hiking cycle than the Federal Reserve, while Eurozone data remain softer than US figures.

item.title: Gold heads for third weekly loss as hawkish Fed rate bets reinforce bearish trend
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains under pressure on Friday as traders assess the latest news about the US-Iran peace deal and the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,150 after hitting a one-week low of $4,121 earlier in the day.
